None of the attempts at answering this question try and solve the technical problem at the heart of it. There is a solution though: IPFS (Inter Planetary File System).

The problem is that there is some data, cat.jpg, and what people do currently is share the address, https://imagehosting.com/cat.jpg. When imagehosting.com goes down, nobody can reach the data anymore. It is either lost or needs to be uploaded to another site, https://imagehosting2.com/cat.jpg.

The solution is to create a hash of the image and that hash provides the unique identification of the image. This is what IPFS does. Instead of everybody downloading the image from the same server/url, people download the image from whoever is hosting it on IPFS. It is a distributed system, so doesn't have a single point of failure. The burden of hosting and network is also distributed amongst people with the file.

IPFS is already well established. There are already examples of IPFS based image hosting sites. If you don't know IPFS you should investigate the links below.
